scope: Source-defined built-in connector catalog after Todoist hosted-MCP migration. Does not inspect user accounts, credentials, configured availability, or live upstream tool lists.
methodology: Pure createRegistry/registerAllProviders introspection with default options, plus source review. No connector runtime, storage, network, or actions executed. X filters are not applied. Todoist remote tool counts remain null because they require runtime discovery. Todoist toolkit actions lists only five known compatibility aliases.
commonMigrationRequirements: Preserve canonical provider/toolkit/action IDs or provide explicit migrations and deprecated aliases.
Preserve connection IDs and account/auth-config scope pins. Validate actual remote user and tenant identity.
Preserve approvals, write-policy overrides, error/indeterminate semantics, redaction, and audit.
Review per-action capability parity rather than inferring it from a directory listing or shared vendor name.
OAuth-native to MCP migration must reconcile authConfigId strategy mismatch and account pin semantics.
Use typed contract adapters for deterministic app consumers, including output fields and pagination.

applicationDependencies.contract: Read every connected account using its pinned connection ID. Preserve normalized event fields, recurrence expansion, time zones, all-day, free/busy, cancellation, RSVP, source URL, and join URL. Calendar failures can make the deck treat a day as open.

Deterministic, typed reads without an LLM. Preserve IDs, titles, state, assignee, priority, dates, URLs, pagination, and toolkitId:externalId chip keys. Jira requests current-user unfinished tasks. Asana selects the first workspace. Notion pages are excluded.

Bot identity and getUpdates enable /start token linking to a saved chat ID and engine connection ID. Delivery expects messageId. Only notifier caller telegram.send_message receives the narrow approval exemption. Native disconnect also removes channel records.
Development live-check tooling refers to these fixed action names and expected results.

platformGaps.summary: Built-in OAuth onboarding uses SDK discovery/DCR and public PKCE metadata. There is no configured static client ID/secret or client-metadata-document path. Directory access may require independent vendor registration or allowlisting.
Custom MCP already supports OAuth, bearer, custom header, and none. Built-in provider metadata is only ID/name/URL and its validator requires OAuth.
Built-ins pin one exact URL. There are no tenant URL templates or generic remote account discovery. Preserving old accountId does not verify sign-in used the same upstream account.

Setup permits one built-in entry per provider. Ingestion registers one same-ID toolkit, and executors capture one client instead of routing by ctx.connection. Google/Microsoft require multiple stable toolkit IDs and per-account dispatch.

Ingestion retains authConfigId but registers bearer auth. A stored OAuth minting config then fails core strategy validation. Clearing the ID without migrating workspace pins is also incorrect. Todoist's former direct-token connections avoid this case.
Only Streamable HTTP is wired. No stdio process installation/lifecycle or legacy SSE client path is implemented.

Tools are discovered on runtime rebuild, without a reviewed contract snapshot or app-level list-changed refresh. Preserve deprecated action names, typed output adapters, data pagination, partial errors, and schema drift tests.

Annotation trust and outward-action name heuristics do not establish full semantics for bulk, financial, admin, or communication tools. Compare capabilities and preserve stricter policy overrides when remote coverage expands.
